title: Lab: Feature Branch Workflow
intro_md: Walk the exact loop you'll use daily on a team: branch, commit, push, and recover from a mistake with revert.

steps.instruction_md: Create and switch to a new branch named `feature/login`.
steps.hint: Modern Git uses `switch -c`; the classic form is `checkout -b`.
git add <path> moves changes into the staging area.

steps.instruction_md: Commit with the message `feat: add login endpoint` (use double quotes).
steps.mock_output:
[feature/login 3f2a1c9] feat: add login endpoint
 1 file changed, 42 insertions(+)

steps.instruction_md: Push the branch to origin and set it as upstream.
steps.mock_output: Branch 'feature/login' set up to track remote branch 'feature/login' from 'origin'.
steps.hint: -u (or --set-upstream) links the local branch to the remote one.

steps.instruction_md: Check which commits exist with a compact one-line graph of all branches.
steps.mock_output:
* 3f2a1c9 (HEAD -> feature/login, origin/feature/login) feat: add login endpoint
* a1b2c3d (main, origin/main) chore: initial commit

steps.instruction_md: The commit `3f2a1c9` broke staging after merge. Undo it safely on the shared branch (no history rewrite), keeping the default commit message (`--no-edit`).
steps.hint: revert adds a new inverse commit — safe on branches others share, unlike reset.
